A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniGeoSeg, GeoSeg-1M and GeoSeg-Bench. Their main text and complete supplementary material are readable, and corresponding equations, tables and figures can be matched despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation and grounding evaluations, component ablations, and supplementary experiments with a DeepSeek-7B backbone.

after.justification: v2 retains original model evaluations and ablations, revises benchmark results, and adds instruction-diversity measurements and a qualitative failure case.

M1.justification: The architecture, task-adaptive text enhancement, latent knowledge memory and progressive task scheduling remain unchanged. Sections 4.1–4.4 and their equations describe the same procedures.

E1.justification: Training sources, segmentation tasks and evaluation datasets remain unchanged, including GeoSeg-Bench, EarthReason, RRSIS-D, SIOR and DIOR-RSVG. The new failure example illustrates the existing contextual-reasoning task rather than introducing distinct task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds HIPIE and SegLLM to the GeoSeg-Bench comparison without GeoSeg-1M fine-tuning. Table 3 removes RemoteSAM from the RRSIS-D comparison, although RemoteSAM remains evaluated elsewhere. The other principal comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The added diversity analysis uses Top50/Top100 2-gram, 3-gram and POS measures, including a 398-sample rural-residential analysis. Existing benchmark protocols are otherwise retained. New Table 14 reports UniGeoSeg batch size 8, conflicting with the retained size 16; the PDFs do not establish which setting produced the revised results.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 10 adds linguistic-diversity analysis addressing potential instruction shortcuts and a hard-negative failure case in Figure 13. The TATE, LKM, scheduling and alternative-backbone ablations are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for model results. The added descriptive diversity percentages do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 revise reported scores: UniGeoSeg's GeoSeg-Bench interactive/referring/reasoning gIoU changes from 76.37/74.25/52.96 to 75.56/74.58/53.12; EarthReason test cIoU/gIoU changes from 75.67/73.12 to 74.61/73.08; RRSIS-D changes from 81.35/72.23 to 79.78/69.25. GeoPixel's RRSIS-D scores also change, and comparator, diversity and failure-case results are added or removed. These are reported-value revisions, without established identical training conditions; zero-shot and ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 and the associated mathematical definitions remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: a million-scale unified dataset, a reasoning-oriented benchmark, the UniGeoSeg framework, and claims of state-of-the-art performance and strong zero-shot generalization.

C2.justification: Section 10 newly interprets linguistic diversity as indicating no obvious superficial-language shortcut. It also explains a failure where UniGeoSeg follows northern-boundary and residential cues while neglecting green-space and road-intersection constraints, adding a concrete limitation.

D1.justification: New Section 11.3/Table 14 documents baseline fine-tuning resolutions, optimizers, learning rates, batch sizes and frozen/trainable components. Section 3.4 newly states patch-level deduplication without establishing a changed split. The abstract changes code/data availability from already released to a future release; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including HIPIE, SegLLM, CrossEarth, Spex and GeoLLaVA-8k, while removing AGMTR, HoliTracer and the AdamW reference. The related-work argument and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged; publication updates to retained works are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: Localized edits add an analysis paragraph, a fine-tuning subsection and acknowledgments, update the contact email, and correct caption typos. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds diversity Table 11, fine-tuning Table 14 and failure-case Figure 13. Tables 2–3 change comparator rows, Table 4 moves, and existing figures are resized with accompanying text reflow. Previously included illustrations and supplementary results remain present under updated numbering.

improvement.justification: The added diversity analysis, explicit failure case and fine-tuning details improve scrutiny of the work. However, v2 removes RemoteSAM from the RRSIS-D comparison without explanation and introduces conflicting batch sizes. Section 5.2 also retains EarthReason gains of 6.65/2.16 points although revised Table 3 supports 5.59/2.12. These unresolved comparison and reproducibility issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
